signals.summary: Hyrox, the standardized functional-fitness race format (sled pushes, wall balls, rowing, running), keeps spreading globally with sustained coverage across major outlets and new demographics picking it up.
signals.why_now: Four independent outlets ran Hyrox pieces in this pull: DW on how it became a global craze, The Times on Chinese pensioners taking it up, plus ABC News and Yahoo explainers on the format. Sustained, multi-outlet, multi-region coverage marks an ongoing wave rather than a single post.

signals.summary: Interest is clustering around optimizing the bedroom environment for sleep: cooler room temperature, morning light exposure, airflow and non-overheating bedding, framed as a ritual space rather than a medical fix.
signals.why_now: University of Utah Health published on cooler bedroom temperature and PsyPost on morning sunlight shifting sleep timing, both fresh (22h/55h), alongside fresh r/sleep threads on window-open-or-closed and memory foam that overheats. The convergence points at a room-and-object environment story.

signals.summary: A wave of mobility, flexibility and functional-strength routines aimed at aging well and staying independent, typically built around simple objects like mats and resistance bands.
signals.why_now: Fresh pieces in this pull include Runner's World on keeping stride power over 50, Kern Valley Sun on seniors' hand strength and mobility, Tom's Guide on bodyweight functional strength, The Telegraph's five-minute flexibility routine, a NYT Well longevity-exercise piece, and Katie Couric Media on staying strong and steady. Multiple independent outlets, several within 48h.

signals.summary: Coverage is coalescing around a mindset shift away from calorie-burn and weight-loss framing toward strength-first, intuitive, low-effort movement, including micro 'exercise snacks' for gym-avoiders.
signals.why_now: Us Weekly ran a fresh (31h) piece on exercise snacks for people who hate the gym, echoing Yahoo Creators on strength training replacing weight loss, WION on intuitive workouts, ELLE on doing less, and Men's Journal on a shift in how we think about health. A consistent conceptual wave, though most anchor pieces are aging.
